# openftgs-synth {VERSION}

Rendered multi-view video scenes with exact ground truth, made to validate
openftgs (an Apache-2.0 clean-room implementation of FreeTimeGS)
without any dataset licensed for non-commercial use.

- **License of this dataset:** CC0-1.0 (see `LICENSE`). Every input asset is CC0-1.0 (see `ASSETS.md`).
- **Generator:** openftgs-synth (GPL-3.0-or-later), Blender {BLENDER} (Cycles, OptiX), ffmpeg 6.1.
- **Rigs and calibrations** are designed from scratch for this dataset. No camera rig,
  calibration or value was copied from Neural3DV, ENeRF-Outdoor or SelfCap.

## Contents

```
LICENSE  DATASET_CARD.md  ASSETS.md  VERSION  SHA256SUMS
n3dv/<scene>/poses_bounds.npy, cam00.mp4 ... camNN.mp4
enerf_outdoor/<scene>/intri.yml, extri.yml, videos/<name>.mp4
selfcap/<seq>-release.tar.gz, <seq>-calib.tar.gz
lossless/<layout>/<scene>/...      the same videos, lossless (libx264rgb -qp 0), plus the calibration files
ground_truth/<scene>/cameras.json, markers.json, pinhole/, depth/, masks/, background/
```

## Scenes

{SCENES_TABLE}

Every scene has a textured static background, rigid objects translating and rotating at
different speeds with one 10-20-frame burst of fast motion, an object that appears and later
disappears, a baked cloth simulation, thin structures (3-12 mm wires, rods and legs), and a
walking CC0 character ("Animated Human" by Quaternius, dressed with CC0 fabric textures).

`tiny` is a smoke test. It is written as `n3dv/tiny` (pinhole frames) and
`enerf_outdoor/tiny` (5-coefficient distortion) from one render. Its selfcap form is the
separate scene `tiny_unsync` (same scene, rig and lens, unsynchronized cameras).
`tiny_d8` and `tiny_d12` repeat `tiny` with the 8- and 12-coefficient models and an
off-centre principal point.

## Conventions

- **World:** right-handed, metres, z up.
- **Cameras:** OpenCV axes (x right, y down, z forward), world-to-camera:
  `x_cam = R x_world + t`, camera centre `C = -R^T t`. `cameras.json` gives the 4x4
  `world_to_camera` and `camera_center`. (Blender cameras look down -z with y up; the
  conversion is `R_c2w_blender = R_c2w_opencv diag(1, -1, -1)`.)
- **Pixels:**
  - YAML files and `K_opencv` use OpenCV's integer pixel centres.
  - `K_continuous` uses the continuous convention: the image spans [0, W] x [0, H] and
    pixel (u, v) is sampled at (u + 0.5, v + 0.5), so `c_continuous = c_opencv + 0.5`.
  - All cameras have square pixels (fx = fy) and no skew.
- **Distortion:** OpenCV models, coefficient order `k1 k2 p1 p2 k3 [k4 k5 k6 [s1 s2 s3 s4]]`.
  It applies to the videos of layouts marked "distorted". The ground-truth images are
  undistorted.
- **Time:** frame n of camera c shows the scene at `t = n/fps - offset_c` seconds.
  `cameras.json` lists n and t for every frame of every camera. Offsets are 0 except in
  unsynchronized scenes, where they are in `sync.json` and lie in [-0.03, +0.03] s.
- **Colour:** Cycles view transform "Standard", sRGB, no look, exposure 0. Frames are
  8-bit sRGB PNG before encoding.
- **Determinism:** no motion blur, rolling shutter, depth of field or auto-exposure. Fixed
  sample count (no adaptive sampling), fixed seed (not animated), fixed OIDN denoiser
  settings, dithering off.

### n3dv layout

- `poses_bounds.npy`: float64 [N, 17], one row per camera in the sorted order of
  `cam00.mp4, cam01.mp4, ...`.
- Each row is a 3x5 matrix `[c0 c1 c2 | centre | hwf]` flattened row-major, then near and
  far bounds. c0, c1, c2 are the camera-to-world rotation's columns pointing down, right
  and back; hwf = (H, W, focal).
- Converting to OpenCV uses camera-to-world rotation `[c1, c0, -c2]`.
- The principal point is the image centre, (W/2, H/2) in the continuous convention.
- Near/far are the 0.1th/99.9th percentiles of the ground-truth depth over all frames of
  that camera, times 0.9/1.1.

### opencv-yaml layout (`enerf_outdoor/`, and inside the selfcap archives)

Written with `cv2.FileStorage`.
- `intri.yml`: `names` (list of strings "0000", ...), `K_<n>` (3x3), `D_<n>` (k x 1),
  `H_<n>`, `W_<n>` (int), and `ccm_<n>` (3x3 identity) in the scene marked ccm.
- `extri.yml`: `R_<n>` (Rodrigues 3x1), `Rot_<n>` (the same rotation as a 3x3 matrix), `T_<n>`
  (3x1, metres, world-to-camera).

### selfcap layout

- `<seq>-release.tar.gz` holds `<seq>-release/videos/<name>.mp4` and
  `<seq>-release/optimized/{intri.yml, extri.yml, sync.json}`.
- `<seq>-calib.tar.gz` holds `<seq>-calib/optimized/{intri.yml, extri.yml, sync.json}`.
- `sync.json` maps camera name to offset in seconds.
- Archives contain regular files only (no directory entries), sorted, with mtime
  2026-10-13T00:00:00Z, uid/gid 0 and gzip mtime 0, so they are reproducible.

### Videos

- **Real-world style:** H.264 (libx264 `-preset slow -crf 18`), yuv420p, BT.709 matrix,
  limited range. Tagged `colorspace=bt709, color_primaries=bt709,
  color_trc=iec61966-2-1 (sRGB), color_range=tv`. Encoded at the scene fps.
- **Lossless:** libx264rgb `-qp 0`, rgb24 input. Each lossless video was checked to decode
  bit-exactly to its source PNG frames.
- ffprobe confirmed every video's frame count and size.

### ground_truth/<scene>/

- `cameras.json`: per camera its name and per-layout names, width, height, `K_opencv`,
  `K_continuous`, distortion model and coefficients, 4x4 `world_to_camera`, centre,
  sync offset, and per frame the decode index n and the time t in seconds.
- `pinhole/<cam>/<n:06d>.png`: the undistorted frames (8-bit sRGB), with K and no
  distortion. For pinhole layouts these are exactly the frames that were encoded.
- `depth/<cam>/<n:06d>.exr`: float32 single channel "Y". Planar z-depth along the optical
  axis in metres, sampled at the pixel centre. 0 means no surface (sky).
- `masks/<cam>/<n:06d>.png`: 8-bit. 255 where a dynamic object (rigid movers, the
  appearing object, cloth, character) is visible at the pixel centre, else 0.
- `background/<cam>.png`: the static scene with every dynamic object hidden (undistorted;
  their shadows are absent too).
- `markers.json`: positions and radius of the emissive validation spheres. They are hidden
  in all normal renders and rendered alone for validation. Also the trajectory of the
  "clock" sphere (`p(t) = p0 + velocity t`) used to check render times.

## How the frames were made

1. Each camera renders an oversized pinhole image (about 15% wider field of view; a larger
   margin where the distortion needs it) at 2x supersampling, as 16-bit sRGB PNG.
2. Pinhole ground truth: crop the margin and box-filter 2x2 in linear light.
3. Distorted frames: for each 2x sub-pixel of the output, normalize with K and invert the
   OpenCV distortion model by Newton iteration (residual below 1e-10 in normalized
   coordinates; achieved about 1e-15). Then project into the oversized render, sample
   bilinearly in linear light, and box-filter 2x2.
4. Depth and masks come from a separate one-sample render at output resolution, sampled at
   the pixel centre (material override: emission = (camera-space z, object pass index)).
5. Unsynchronized cameras are each rendered at their own times. The baked cloth cache and
   the animation are evaluated at sub-frame times.

Render settings: {RENDER_SETTINGS}

## Validation

All checks are scripts in the openftgs-synth repository (`validate/`) and passed for every
scene before release.

{VALIDATION_TABLE}

1. **Marker projection:** markers rendered alone (linear EXR, many samples). The
   intensity-weighted centroid matches the projection of the sphere centre through
   `K_opencv` and the pose (pinhole frames), and through `cv2.projectPoints` with D
   (distorted frames). A half-pixel convention error would show as about 0.5 px.
2. **Undistort round trip:** `cv2.undistort(distorted, K, D)` against the pinhole frames,
   excluding a 3 px border. Also computed with the principal point moved by 0.5 px, to show
   the test would catch a convention error. `tiny*` scenes at 160x120 are judged against the
   bilinear interpolation floor at that resolution, since cv2's bilinear resampling alone
   adds more than a few levels on their textures.
3. **poses_bounds:** each row converted with `[c1, c0, -c2]` reproduces the ground-truth
   world-to-camera pose to 1e-9.
4. **YAML read-back:** `cv2.FileStorage` reads back K, D, H, W, ccm, R, Rot and T exactly;
   Rodrigues(R) equals Rot to 1e-9.
5. **Times:** `cameras.json` times equal n/fps - offset; `sync.json` equals `cameras.json`;
   every Blender job was rendered at the camera's own time. The clock sphere's image
   position recovers each render time to within 0.1 px of image motion.
6. **Archives and checksums:** each archive lists exactly the expected members, and
   `SHA256SUMS` covers every file in the dataset.
